native_result.query: How does the effect of increasing education expenditure on per capita GDP compare between developing countries and countries in Sub-Saharan Africa?
native_result.HypoA: The effect of increasing education expenditure on per capita GDP is more pronounced in developing countries outside of Sub-Saharan Africa compared to those within it
native_result.HypoB: The effect of education expenditure on per capita economic output is substantially stronger in magnitude and responsiveness in developing countries (LMC) than in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), with developing countries exhibiting approximately sixfold higher output elasticity to education expenditure variations and higher transmission into secondary school human capital compared to SSA.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1. Data ingestion and reshaping: Converted wide-format panel (12 series x 41 years) into long tidy panel. 2. Econometric modeling: Estimated log-log elasticities and linear marginal effects for both LMC and SSA across overlapping window (2011-2015). 3. Interaction and control models: Tested difference in slopes (interaction term log_edu_exp * is_LMC) controlling for exports growth and enrollment. 4. Long-term human capital transmission: Evaluated multi-decade trends (1975-2015) in primary/secondary school enrollment and labor force participation to explain structural divergence.

sub_hypo.text: The effect of increasing education expenditure on per capita GDP is more pronounced in developing countries outside of Sub-Saharan Africa compared to those within it.
sub_hypo.context: Developing countries outside Sub-Saharan Africa compared with developing countries within Sub-Saharan Africa.
sub_hypo.relations: Increasing education expenditure has a stronger effect on per capita GDP in developing countries outside Sub-Saharan Africa than in those within it.

gold_sub_hypo.full_hypo: The effect of increasing education expenditure on per capita GDP is more pronounced in developing countries outside of Sub-Saharan Africa compared to those within it

sub_hypo.text: Education expenditure has a substantially stronger effect on per capita economic output in Lower Middle Income Countries (LMC) than in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), with approximately sixfold higher output elasticity in LMC.
sub_hypo.context: Comparison of LMC and SSA over the overlapping estimation window 2011–2015, controlling for exports growth and school enrollment.
sub_hypo.relations: Country group moderates the education expenditure–output relationship: LMC exhibits substantially larger linear marginal effects and approximately sixfold higher log-log output elasticity than SSA. Slope differences are tested using the interaction log_edu_exp * is_LMC, controlling for exports growth and enrollment.

sub_hypo.text: Education expenditure has higher transmission into secondary school human capital in LMC than in SSA.
sub_hypo.context: Comparison of LMC and SSA, with long-term human capital transmission evaluated through trends over 1975–2015.
sub_hypo.relations: Education expenditure translates more strongly into secondary school human capital in LMC than in SSA. Multi-decade primary and secondary enrollment and labor force participation trends are evaluated to explain structural divergence.
